incident_description:
The consumer contracted an infection from contact dermatitis due to the toxic dyes in the shoes.  The consumer went through multiple toe amputations, a lower leg amputation and then died of sepsis as a result of the infection on February 5, 2023.

ADDENDUM:  per attached letter from submitter/attorney
July 16, 2024


VIA EMAIL: clearinghouse@cpsc.gov US Consumer Product Safety Commission ATTN: Reports
4330 East-West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Re:	Clarks Americas Recall 23-036 Notification of injury and death

To Whom It May Concern:

We are a bit confused by the refusal to post our notification of claim but hopefully this letter will resolve all issues.

Benzidine is a well-established carcinogen and most of the scientific and medical journal research in the last couple of decades has focused on its carcinogenic properties, but as early as the 19_, peer reviewed journal articles determined that benzidine caused increase rates of contact dermatitis in factory workers who were working with benzidine dyes. These journal articles established that contact dermatitis is seen in a statistically significant number of persons (such as factory workers) who are repetitively exposed to the dyes, without personal protection over the skin. [REDACTED] wore the Clarks shoes that were laden with benzidine dyes without socks on her foot and wore these slip-on shoes for a number of weeks prior to developing her contact dermatitis. It is well established that persons suffering contact dermatitis can develop infection on the affected area. [REDACTED] medical records indicated that she suffered the first infection on a topical superficial area of her right toes, where she developed an outbreak, which later became septic and she died as a result of this original infection.

All of her medical records were provided to [REDACTED], an endocrinologist with over 30 years experience in treating patients with diabetic ulcers as well as other afflictions. His comprehensive report is attached with his conclusions that this was a contact dermatitis which became infected and then septic.

Although not attached to this submission, we have consulted with both a internal medicine doctor with a toxicology degree, as well as with a wound care specialist and both of these specialists have concluded that this was a contact dermatitis irritation/infection caused by benzidine dye exposure and irritation.
 
We are also attaching a series of medical journal articles relating to contact dermatitis suffered by workers who were repetitively exposed to benzidine dyes. If you have any further questions about whether this exposure to benzidine dye caused the infection and sepsis in our client please feel free to reach out to me.

A listing of all materials supplied to you is attached on an index.

Very truly yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer died as a result of sepsis from an infection caused by contact dermatitis due to toxic dyes in the shoes.

I was wearing skechers shapeups which I got as an early birthday present and I was wearing them for the first day.  The first words out of my mouth were"these stupid shoes!" I also knew something was wrong because my leg didn't look right. Every little move I made I could hear the bones making a crackling noise. I had to hold it until the ambulance came in Marshfield and they brought me to South Shore in Weymouth.  I was in shock the whole ride.  They took x-rays( which I have) and saw the two broken bones (spiral fractures)
in my leg.  [REDACTED] did surgery and put in a rod and two pins.  I stayed there after for four days.  Then after that I went to a rehab for almost 2 months. There I did physical therapy 2 hours a day 6 days a week. I went through excruciating pain through this ordeal I'm happy to say Im home now and for you to know the skecher shapeups might look cool yet they are very dangerous and I would definately take them off the market, my opinion.  Thanks!

incident_description:
On 5/2/2014, I was home for lunch and preparing for an overnight trip.  I picked up my two Saddleback leather satchels (medium and large sized) by the shoulder straps to take them out to my car.  As I got the strap for the large bag to shoulder height and prepared to place the strap on my shoulder, the heavy metal clasp that connects the strap to the bag disconnected from the side of the bag facing forward.  This caused a weighted pendulum effect, swinging the strap up from the bag towards my face, with the metal clasp violently striking me in the teeth and loosening my four upper front teeth and causing them to hurt badly.

I have a number of Saddleback bags, and have had the clasps disconnect a number of times in the past due to the design, but never had the strap strike me before.  It has always been clear to me since the first incident that these straps need to have more than a latching mechanism - they need a latching AND locking mechanism.  However, it never occurred to me that the disconnecting clasp issue could cause bodily harm in addition to possibly damaging the contents of the bags.  

I no longer feel safe picking up my bags as intended as a result of this.  I contacted Saddleback via their web contact form that I have used in the past and previously gotten replies in a couple hours.  They have not replied in the two days that have passed.  In the meantime, in order to use my bags and feel I can do so safely, I have tied the clasps to the bags with para-cord.  I do no feel this is a good long term solution since these bags are expensive and supposedly warrantied for 100 years.  I had also never thought it was possible to be beat up by a bag before, but now I know it can happen with these bags.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (loosened teeth and pain), and the description notes prior occurrences of clasp disconnection, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

She was taken to the Mercy West hospital by ambulance and later transferred to the Jewish hospital because she had bleeding on her brain.  Caller stated that she was admitted to the hospital for 2 days for observation and then released for follow up with their physician. Caller stated that his spouse also received bruises to her body.
(6/29/21) Caller stated that he contacted the company and they advised that someone would contact him but no one has contacted him as yet. Caller is concerned that this umbrella is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

I believe that the stand for this product could be made safer by bolting or strapping the black weights at the base together. As you can see by the pictures included, the outer weights were completely shed from the base. Once the weight is detached from the base stand, it can tip over very easily. It took only about a second or two for the umbrella to start to rotate, start to come down, knock my wife against the wall and make a final rotation of 180 degrees before falling on my deck railing. She was unable to get up and was put in a neck brace and onto a stretcher then taken to the hospital by ambulance. 

I contacted Simply Shade, the manufacturer, on Tuesday, June 29, 2021. Their response was to contact me by text on Thursday, July 1, that said, 'Hello, this is Simply Shade customer service. How can I help you today?' I texted back that the umbrella fell over and that my wife was taken to the hospital and I needed to talk with somebody. As of this writing, July 7, 2021, I have not yet gotten a reply from them. I had already explained the whole situation to the original person I had left a message with on Tuesday.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bleeding on the brain and bruises) requiring hospitalization, but no death was reported.

incident_description: On Friday, March 9, 2012, my wife was wearing a pair of Skechers Shape-up toning shoes. She walked a few feet up an incline in the back yard to retrieve a piece of plastic that had blown into the yard, and when she turned around (foot at right angles to the slope), her foot rolled and her ankle immediately dislocated and fractured. The paramedics arrived in about 10 minutes, and when they saw the shoe she had on they shook their head and stated that they get many emergency calls related to that shoe type and make. This was the first that I had heard that there was a problem with this type shoe, though I had purchased a pair myself and did not like them, because I noticed a tendency of instability when I walked across a driveway sloping downward. Upon reaching the ER of the Cottonwood Hospital, the orthopedic surgeon [REDACTED] also commented about the many incidents he had seen that were related to the wearing of this shoe, and said they were dangerous. X-rays showed the dislocation, and after a pain blocking shot, he "reduced" the dislocation, and X-rays again were taken which showed fractures of both side bones in the ankle. The operating room was scheduled, so he put a cast on her foot, and scheduled surgery for Monday, March 12. Following surgery, her foot again was put in a cast, with a follow-up scheduled for March 27. Her intense pain initially was to be controlled by Hydro-Codone, which was not successful, so prescription was changed to Percocet, which has been controlling her pain.
justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated and fractured ankle requiring surgery and pain management, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The paramedics and surgeon noted many similar incidents, suggesting the likelihood is likely (4).

incident_description:
Toner shoes.


I waited almost a year after the shape ups came out to try them.  I figured if there were problems they would get reported and the product would be pulled.

They claimed the shoes reduce feet and back pain by improving strength and circulation.

They state they reduce the impact on joints and lower back and have maximum shock absorption.

I did not buy them as exercise equipment.  I bought them because they made it sound like they would help with pain by building up muscles needed for proper posture and stamina.

When I adjusted to them I threw away all my regular shoes and only had toner shoe.
After about 9 months,  I could not walk up or down stairs without fear of falling.

I went to a doctor who repaired a tear in my right knee. It did not fix the problem but I am able to do stairs with pain but not fear of falling. It was his opinion that I will need a complete knee replacement in about 5 years.  There is already very slight bone on bone.

My left knee was also affected but did not require surgery.


I am doing this complaint because I feel they should warn people with joint issues to stay away from their product.  They are promoting them as a way to help.  They did not and I honesty believe they caused the damage to my knees. 

I also see that they are making them for children.  I fear for the safety of the children who do wear only shape ups.  If they cause damage to adults what are they going to do to developing children?
justification: The user experienced knee injuries requiring medical intervention, including surgery, which qualifies as an injury (Severity 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) as the incident occurred after prolonged use but may not be common for all users.

I walked out the front door, walked down one or two steps and my ankle rolled causing me to fall the rest of the way down the stairs. My daughter drove me to the ER where I was diagnosed with fracture of the Distal Fibula-which is at the end of the fibula and is one of the bones that support the ankle joint. I also have bruising and swelling around my knee. I had xrays taken on April 6, 2012 and there are no fractures. However torn muscles have not been ruled out and a MRI may be taken at a later date.

Today, April 10, I met with an orthopedic surgeon had repeat xrays taken and was told that surgery is probable due to bone displacement. I have a follow up appointment on April 17 to make a final decision. In the meantime, my foot is in a cast and I am to remain off of it unless using the restroom, bathing or traveling to doctor appointments.
justification: The incident resulted in a fracture and potential torn muscles, requiring medical attention and probable surgery, which qualifies as an injury.
